title: end-user-cost-consent-flow-scratchpad
content:
Context / quick pitch:
We surface a lightweight, end-user-facing consent and cost preview flow when an application is about to trigger high-cost inference (long prompts, multimodal, large model). The goal: reduce surprise billing, improve trust, and give product teams an easy opt-in UX to present tradeoffs (latency, cost, fidelity).

Why now:
- Customers keep asking for an out-of-the-box pattern to avoid customer complaints when tokens/embeddings spike.
- Console + API telemetry shows a long tail of sessions that blow cost budgets.
- Compliance teams prefer explicit consent for billable features in some regulated accounts.

Primary goals:
- Give end users a clear, contextual cost/latency preview before a 'risky' request executes.
- Provide product teams (on Redwood) a configurable widget and API hooks to control thresholds, copy, and fallback behavior.
- Track user accept/decline events for analytics and refunding flows.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Full per-token live meter for end users (we'll show estimates).
- Billing reconciliation automation (finance side handles refunds outside this MVP).

Personas:
- Product manager at a SaaS (PM) who wants to reduce surprise costs for customers and keep conversion high.
- End user (power user) who needs one large export/analysis and is willing to accept a charge.
- Admin (account owner) who sets global preferences for the org.

Key UX hypotheses to test:
- A simple one-line estimate + max-possible cost reduces calls that trigger disputable charges by >40%.
- Explicit consent increases trust and reduces support contacts.
- Showing a lower-fidelity fallback option (cheaper but slower/shorter output) maintains conversion vs hard block.

Rough flow (MVP):
1) Detection: an API/proxy layer flags requests that are likely to exceed a configured per-request cost threshold (tokens * model-rate estimate + embedding ops).
2) Preflight response: client receives 403-like signal with metadata: {estimated_cost_usd, expected_latency_s, suggested_fallbacks[]}.
3) Console widget: embedded modal with summary copy, 2 CTAs: "Proceed (charge)", "Run cheaper variant" and tertiary "Cancel".
4) If Proceed: client posts explicit consent token -> we execute original request and log consent event.
5) If fallback chosen: route to cheaper model/quantized variant and mark in telemetry.

Minimum viable API contract notes (sketch):
- Preflight endpoint: POST /v1/requests/preflight with request payload (model, prompt_size_tokens, features) -> returns {estimate_usd, latency_ms_est, fallback_options, consent_required: boolean, consent_id}  (consent_id short-lived)
- Consent endpoint: POST /v1/requests/consent with consent_id + user_info -> returns {execute_token} or error
- Telemetry: events: consent_shown, consent_accepted, consent_declined, fallback_used, consent_expired

Product/user stories (MVP):
- As an end user, I see a clear estimate and can choose a cheaper option before being charged.
- As a PM, I can set a per-route threshold in Console that triggers preflight checks.
- As an admin, I can disable end-user prompts and force server-side auto-fallbacks for some orgs.
- As an engineer, I can retrieve audit logs of consent events for last 90 days.

Acceptance criteria (first pass):
- Preflight endpoint returns deterministic estimate within +/- 25% for 95% of flagged requests.
- Consent flow completes and the original request executes within SLO (median extra latency < 200ms for the handshake).
- Console allows toggling threshold and customizing modal copy & fallback options.
- Events recorded and visible in per-route telemetry.

Telemetry / metrics to capture:
- preflight_trigger_rate per-route
- consent_shown_rate (ratio of triggers to shown modals)
- consent_accept_rate (of shown)
- fallback_select_rate
- mean_cost_of_consented_requests vs baseline
- support_ticket_reduction (lagging)

Edge cases / corner concerns:
- Bots & automated clients: how do we do consent for programmatic flows? (offer server-to-server bypass with org-level consent toggle).
- Race conditions for streaming/real-time features where waiting for consent is unacceptable (we should support progressive output: first n tokens free, then stop for consent).
- GDPR / privacy: consent content must be stored with minimal PII and purgeable upon request.
- Refund logic: need clear handoff to finance; include link to ledger id in consent event.

Implementation notes / infra impact:
- Small new preflight service or add preflight to existing routing layer. Needs accurate cost-estimator that mirrors billing rates (quantization, hardware, model variant).
- Short-lived consent tokens must be cryptographically verifiable and limited lifetime (1–5 min).
- UI: packaged React widget for Console + embeddable JS snippet for customers building their own UI.
- Rate limits: preflight calls should be cheap; sample in high volume paths to avoid extra cost loops.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha: internal-only with a few QA product teams + experiments on sandbox orgs.
- Beta: opt-in in Console for self-serve customers; provide widget and API docs.
- GA: enable per-route thresholds for enterprise and add tenant-level enforcement for regulated accounts.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should we allow merchants (customers) to bill on behalf of end-users and how to model that? (complicated, put in backlog)
- UX copy test matrix: "estimate" vs "possible charge" phrasing. Need microcopy A/B experiments.
- How to price the consent flow itself (do we charge preflight calls?) — probably free but must watch abuse.
- Server-side bypass for headless clients: require org-admin API key flag + audit.

Next steps / TODOs (short list):
- [ ] Spike: implement estimator prototype in routing layer (owner: Mika)
- [ ] Draft Console modal copy and screenshot (owner: Evelyn)
- [ ] Wire up telemetry schema in Observability (owner: Noah)
- [ ] Create Confluence page with full UX mockups and privacy checklist

Notes to self (brain-dump):
- Keep the wording consumer-friendly. Avoid showing raw token counts (too nerdy).
- Fallback options should include a "fast summary" cheap mode that lets user get partial output quickly so they can decide to pay.
- Consider integration with Dedicated / Private: orgs may want to surface internal cost in different currency (credits).
- If we can estimate carbon footprint per-request cheaply, it's an optional badge for some enterprise buyers (parking lot).

Slack threads / references to copy/paste:
- #pm-cost-safety thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CTEST12345/p1689100000000
- Related GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/482 (contains small react modal)

Last thought: the psychology matters — people are okay paying if they feel in control. The role of Redwood is to make the UX low friction for product teams to adopt and for users to quickly understand tradeoffs.

(END)
